hero_subtitle: Explore how Coventry City Council manages public money. £2.72B tracked across 617K transactions spanning 9 financial years.
publisher_bio: This website was created by Tom Pickup, Reform UK county councillor for Padiham and Burnley West and Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care at Lancashire County Council. He is also parish councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw. Tom builds transparency tools that make public spending data easier to check.
publisher_titles: County Councillor for Padiham and Burnley West
Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Lancashire County Council
Parish Councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw
publisher_quote: It's your money. The more people understand where it goes, the better.

doge_context.political_control_summary: Coventry City Council went into no overall control after May 2026 elections. Labour remained the largest party but lost majority — seats plummeted from 39 to 24. Reform UK gained 18 seats to reach 20; Conservatives 6, Greens 4. 28 seats needed for majority — none achieved. Hung council with coalition negotiations.

political_control.tenure_note: NOC after May 2026; Labour largest at 24/54 (lost from 39), Reform UK 20 (+18). 28 needed for majority.
